first.rationale: Onboarding completion is directly deteriorating, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing onboarding or signup friction improves completion, activation, and early adoption. This is currently the strongest sustainable-growth path. Verify memory_86 because its evidence must support downstream qualified revenue rather than only early funnel metrics; verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the strongest competing response but carries greater risk to retention, margins, and customer quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable adoption. Promotional pricing is rejected despite qualified-revenue lift because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. Uncertainty remains because the onboarding source does not directly report long-term qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Keep the shortened-onboarding experiment despite the competitor’s deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue and current onboarding weakness. Do not respond with promotional pricing: the verified discounted cohort had 30-day retention -12% and failed to survive first renewal. The doubled churn conversations are a material unresolved risk, but no available evidence supports discounting as a sustainable countermeasure, and no verification capacity remains.
